collapse_rule: Sum the ensembled probabilities of intermediate classes assigned to each reported group, then select the largest collapsed probability.

selection_method.scope: The 280 core taxa represented in discriminator training; rare-extension taxa and discriminator test records were excluded.
selection_method.group_count_selection: A validation-only constrained variance-aware hierarchy compared candidate group counts using separately reported predictive recoverability, variance-standardized separation, and balance constraints.
selection_method.core_assignment_freeze: After selecting k=11, core assignments were frozen from 500 within-taxon bootstrap replicates using the modal consensus partition.
selection_method.reported_collapse_selection: The fixed balanced 11-to-6 validation candidate was selected from admissible collapses to limit the largest record and taxon shares while retaining comparable macro_f1 and minimum-group F1.
selection_method.rare_taxon_assignment: Taxa with 50–499 total records were assigned to the nearest fixed k11 group prototype using deterministic development-only centroids; held-out rare-taxon records were not used.
selection_method.rare_taxon_split: The minimum support of 50 records was applied before an 80% development and 20% held-out split; consequently, rare_development_counts begins at 40 and rare_test_counts begins at 10.
selection_method.test_use: Neither discriminator nor stage-two test records were used to select k, define core groups, select the collapse, assign rare taxa, or select checkpoints.

notes: The 11 intermediate groups are model labels; the six reported groups are a fixed probability-sum collapse.
The balanced collapse was selected from the admissible validation candidates to limit the largest record and taxon shares while retaining comparable macro-F1 and minimum-group F1.
Rare-taxon assignments were frozen from development-only taxon centroids before held-out evaluation.
Group identifiers are arbitrary and do not represent botanical ranks or ecological functions.
